$comment: The source of sf-mail-structure's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js); standard simai.smart-component 1.4, vocabulary 1.1.5. Written for simai/ui-mail by the owner's decision D31 of 2026-10-29: a product repository makes no component set of its own, the shared components live in ui-pro. Written by hand in the 1.4 form on the shape of sf-mail-letters; x-decisions says how each point was decided.

rows.x-markup: a property (a host has objects), or the JSON island a server prints; title and summary are text, never markup.
rows.summary: The blocks in the letter's order, one row each: {id, title, summary, icon, family}. family marks a place every letter has (header, footer): it does not move and nothing lands outside it.

selected.summary: The chosen block; empty means the letter's own settings are chosen.

inserter-items.summary: The kinds an insertion point between rows offers, as sf-sortable takes them: {value, label, icon, caption, keywords} and {type: 'heading', label}. Empty shows no insertion points.

select.x-summary: a row or the settings row was chosen (vocabulary §5 select); id is empty for the letter's settings, keyboard says it came from Enter or Space, so a host can move focus to the panel.
select.summary: This block was chosen: {id, keyboard}. An empty id is the letter's own settings.

move.x-summary: a drag, Alt+arrows or the ⋯ menu asked to move a block (vocabulary §5 move). index is the final place, already kept between the pinned places. A pinned row never sends it.
move.summary: Move this block to this place: {id, index}.

insert.x-summary: an insertion point asked for a new block of a kind at a place, already kept between the pinned places (a verb of this element, as sf-sortable-insert).
insert.summary: Add a new block of this kind at this place: {type, index}.

add.x-summary: «Добавить блок» or the empty card's button: a block was asked for, the place is the host's (vocabulary §5 add).
add.summary: A block was asked for; the host decides where.

duplicate.summary: Make a copy of this block: {id}.

delete.x-summary: «Удалить» under ⋯ or the Delete key (vocabulary §5 delete {ids}); one row is one block, so ids holds it and id names it. A pinned row never sends it.

replace.x-summary: «Сменить вариант…» under the ⋯ of a pinned place (vocabulary §5 replace, as sf-mail-library's): the host shows the variants.
replace.summary: Another variant of this place was asked for: {family}.

select.x-summary: choose as a row does; refused unknown
select.summary: Choose a block as its row does; no id chooses the letter's settings; refused unknown for a block not given.

move.x-summary: move to a place or by steps, kept between the pinned places; refused unknown, pinned, unchanged
move.summary: Move a block to index or by steps, kept between the pinned places; refused pinned for a place, unchanged when it would stay.

x-returns.description: {outcome: applied} or {outcome: refused, reason: unknown | pinned | unchanged}

insert.x-summary: what an insertion point does; refused unknown for a kind not offered
insert.summary: Ask for a new block as an insertion point does; refused unknown for a kind not offered.

add.summary: Ask for a block as «Добавить блок» does.

duplicate.summary: Ask for a copy of a block; refused pinned for a place.

x-returns.description: {outcome: applied} or {outcome: refused, reason: unknown | pinned}

delete.x-summary: what «Удалить» does: sends delete; refused unknown, pinned
delete.summary: Ask to remove a block: sends delete; refused pinned for a place.

x-returns.description: {outcome: applied} or {outcome: refused, reason: unknown | pinned}

replace.x-summary: what «Сменить вариант…» does; refused unknown, not-pinned
replace.summary: Ask for another variant of a pinned place; refused not-pinned for a block.

x-returns.description: {outcome: applied} or {outcome: refused, reason: unknown | not-pinned}

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

accessibility.x-keys: the settings row, then the list as one tab stop on the chosen row; arrows go between rows, Enter and Space choose, Alt+arrows move, Delete removes, Shift+F10 opens ⋯; a held row is sf-sortable's own keyboard; a refusal of a pinned place is said in a status line

x-summary: The structure of a letter in SIMAI Email Editor: the letter's settings, one row per block, and a way to add a block. A row chooses, moves, copies and removes its block; a point between rows asks for a new block there; the header and the footer stay pinned. The element holds no letter and changes none; it says what the person asked for.

x-source.converted: written by hand (D31, 2026-10-30) from the editor's own list, so the words, the keys and the pinned rules are the ones the editor proved

x-decisions: names: sf-mail-structure, as the dispatcher's plan names it (PACKAGE-2-REALIGNED).
shape: a leaf that places sf-sortable, sf-button, sf-icon-button, sf-empty-state and one sf-context-menu as its own markup.
pinned places: the element keeps them, not the host: a drop or an insertion beyond one is reported as the nearest place, which is what the editor did by hand.
events: select, move, add, delete and replace are vocabulary §5 verbs; insert and duplicate are verbs of this element. None is cancelable: the element changes no letter.

$comment: The structure draws its marks as sf-icon, its ⋯ as sf-icon-button and the empty
card as sf-empty-state with an sf-button; a tag it renders is a tag it fetches.
sf-sortable is fetched after the page is ready: arriving before this element
draws, it would take the printed rows as its own first paint and drop them.
The ⋯ menu opens in sf-context-menu on a press, so it is fetched then too, and
the element waits for it before opening it.

id.description: The block's id: what the events carry.

summary.description: What it holds, a second line drawn as text.

family.description: The place it stands in, when it is one: header or footer.

choice.const: A row dispatches sf-mail-structure-select {id, keyboard}; a drag or Alt+arrows sf-mail-structure-move {id, index}; an insertion point sf-mail-structure-insert {type, index}; «Добавить блок» sf-mail-structure-add {}; ⋯ sf-mail-structure-duplicate {id}, sf-mail-structure-delete {ids, id} and, on a pinned place, sf-mail-structure-replace {family}. The element changes nothing: the host does, and passes rows back.

forbidden_client_responsibilities: changing the letter or its blocks
reading or writing the letter store

untrusted_inputs: block titles and summaries (drawn as text)

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-mail-structure wherever a person sees and rearranges the blocks of a letter in SIMAI Email Editor.
do_not: Do not change the letter in the element; listen for its events and do it in the host
Do not keep a block before the pinned header or after the pinned footer; the element already reports the nearest place
Do not draw a second «Добавить блок» beside it

accessibility.focus: The settings row comes first, then the list as one tab stop on the chosen row. ⋯ is named «Действия с блоком: <name>», so two rows never sound alike. The chosen row is aria-current, not by colour alone.
